rem:lichnerowicz-wkb-corollary: Remark Lichnerowicz identity reduces the \Phi_q-WKB conjecture. The categorical Lichnerowicz identity provides the gauge Hessian at the categorical-instanton saddle. This q-Laplacian \Delta_ abla^q equals \mathfrak{D}_ abla^2 on the parallel-Reeb background. The Pfaffian structure on chiral spinors converts - frac{1}{2}\log \det \Delta_ abla^q = -\log \det |\mathfrak{D}_ abla| = - frac{1}{2}\log \det \mathfrak{D}_ abla, recovering the WKB S_1 formula.
rem:lichnerowicz-q-correction: Remark The \tfrac14\mathrm{Sc}_q correction term and its vanishing on the Bring background. The q-scalar curvature \mathrm{Sc}_q = R + O(\hbar_q) encodes both the classical scalar curvature and the anomaly contribution from d_q^2 \neq 0. The O(\hbar_q) correction adds a contact-curvature term on a non-flat aether. On the contact-flat Bring background, both contributions vanish, yielding \Delta_\nabla^q = \mathfrak{D}_\nabla^2.
rem:q-harmonic-particle:
Remark Particles as q-harmonic forms: the logical chain. By the self-adjointness and positive-definiteness of \Delta_q, a form \alpha is q-harmonic (\Delta_q \alpha = 0) if and only if it is simultaneously q-closed and q-coclosed:

  d_q\alpha = 0 \quad\text{and}\quad \delta_q\alpha = 0.

A particle is a field configuration in perfect equilibrium with respect to the q-deformed geometry. The fermion--boson decomposition classifies particles by their vertical component under the weight decomposition. Bosons are purely horizontal (\alpha_V = 0); fermions have non-trivial vertical part.

The logical chain is: \text{QOU} \to \text{\(q\)-exterior derivative} \to \text{\(q\)-codifferential} \to \text{\(q\)-Laplacian} \to \text{particle} \to \text{boson \(\oplus\) fermion}.
rem:brings-geometric-connection: Remark Bring's-surface geometric realisation. The geometric structures of the q-Laplacian, fermion--boson decomposition, and contact affine chart manifest concretely on the Bring surface. The contact structure \varTheta, Reeb vector field \xi, and aether parameter q reduce to explicit formulas on a genus-4 Riemann surface with S_5 symmetry. The abstract equilibrium \Delta_q \alpha = 0 reduces to computable eigenvalue problems, and the boson--fermion split becomes a Hodge decomposition of the harmonic space.
rem:complex-aether-interpretation:
Remark Complex aether parameter and the observability constraint. For a complex aether parameter q = |q|e^{i\theta_q}, the quantum Planck constant is \hbar_q = 1 - |q|^{-1} e^{-i\theta_q}. When \theta_q \neq 0, \hbar_q acquires an imaginary part, and the q-equilibrium mixes amplitudes with phases.

The observability axiom demands positive-definiteness of the Haar functional h_q. This requires d_q^\dagger to be the formal adjoint of d_q, which holds if and only if q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}. Relaxing the observability axiom gives the phase \theta_q geometric meaning:

  1. Complex q contributes a continuous relative phase between over- and under-crossings.
  2. Chirality reversal acts as a continuous rotation in the \theta_q-circle.
  3. The non-Hermitian q-Laplacian produces complex eigenvalues, generating a probability current along the Reeb fibre.

The specialisation at root-of-unity q_0 = e^{\pi i / \kappa} is complex. Root-of-unity categories carry a modified quantum trace \mathrm{tr}_q restoring a non-degenerate pairing without requiring Hilbert-space positive-definiteness, forming a consistent algebraic sector outside the strict observability axiom.
sec:instanton-intro: The gauge term of the canonical action takes its extremal value when the curvature is \star_q-self-dual. This section defines the categorical instanton and reads off its consequences for the categorical Lagrangian on-shell.
def:categorical-instanton: Definition Categorical instanton. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, au) be a quantum observable universe with connection abla and q-Hodge star \star_q. The connection abla is an instanton if its curvature F_ abla \in \Omega^2(A) is \star_q-self-dual: \star_q F_ abla = F_ abla.
rem:categorical-instanton-remark: Remark Instantons and the self-dual projection. Equivalently, the curvature of an instanton factors through the self-dual projection of \Omega^2(A).
prop:categorical-instanton-exists: Proposition Existence of categorical instantons. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with q-Hodge star \star_q. There exists a categorical connection \nabla whose curvature F_\nabla is \star_q-self-dual.
prf:categorical-instanton-exists: Proof Proof of existence of categorical instantons. The trivial connection \nabla_0 = d has F_{\nabla_0} = 0, which is by definition \star_q-self-dual; hence the zero instanton exists. Non-trivial instantons exist on \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-bundles over the CR realisation (example) via categorical descent of the classical instanton of A. A. Belavin, A. M. Polyakov, A. S. Schwartz, and Yu. S. Tyupkin (BPST) [belavin-polyakov-schwartz-tyupkin1975] (self-duality, proved below).
prop:categorical-instanton-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of categorical instantons (moduli). Two categorical instantons \nabla_1 and \nabla_2 of the same topological charge c_2(\nabla_i) = k \in H^4 coincide up to a categorical gauge transformation g \in \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau):

  \nabla_2 \;=\; g \cdot \nabla_1 \cdot g^{-1} + g\,dg^{-1}.

The categorical instanton moduli space \mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{inst}}_k is parameterised by H^4.
prf:categorical-instanton-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of categorical instantons up to gauge. The proof strategy uses characteristic classes and gauge equivalence. The second Chern class c_2 completely classifies the solutions up to gauge transformations. Consequently, any two instantons with the same c_2 coincide, and the moduli space of solutions is faithfully parameterized by H^4.

Two self-dual connections with the same c_2 differ by an element of \ker(d_{\nabla_1}) acting on the fibre — i.e. by an automorphism of A preserving the Frobenius--Hopf structure. Such automorphisms form the categorical gauge group \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau). Thus \nabla_2 - \nabla_1 \in \Omega^1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) is a horizontal form on which the self-duality constraint acts by definition (both connections are self-dual), so it integrates to a gauge transformation g realising \nabla_2 = g \cdot \nabla_1 \cdot g^{-1} + g\,dg^{-1}. The moduli \mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{inst}}_k is the quotient of the self-dual connection space by this gauge action.
lem:categorical-irreducible: Lemma Irreducibility from observability. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Any categorical instanton \nabla is irreducible: \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1},\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.
prf:categorical-irreducible:
Proof Proof of Irreducibility from observability. Suppose s \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) is a non-zero invariant morphism. The following diagram commutes:

\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "s"] \ar[dr, "0"']
  & \mathrm{Ad}(A) \ar[d, "\int_A|_{\mathrm{Ad}}"] \\
  & \mathbf{1}
\end{tikzcd}

Since \mathrm{Ad}(A) is the trace-free part of A \otimes A^*, the Frobenius form \int_A vanishes on it: \int_A \circ s = 0. But \int_A is non-degenerate by the observability axiom, so s = 0.
prop:categorical-self-duality:
Proposition Categorical self-duality. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Every connection \nabla that is a critical point of the categorical Yang--Mills functional

  S[\nabla] =  \int_A\!\bigl(\star_q(F_\nabla) \cdot F_\nabla\bigr)

is an instanton.

The argument is the Bogomolny decomposition, given in the proof below.
prf:categorical-self-duality:
Proof Proof of Categorical self-duality. By the Bogomolny decomposition in the dagger category,

  \int_A(F_\nabla^* \cdot F_\nabla)
  =  2\int_A({F_\nabla^-}^* \cdot F_\nabla^-)
        + \int_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q F_\nabla),

where the second term is topological (determined by the class [F_\nabla] \in \Omega^2(A)/\mathrm{exact}). Minimising S[\nabla] forces F_\nabla^- = 0, which is exactly the self-duality condition.
rem:instanton-on-shell:
Remark On-shell simplification: instanton backgrounds. On an instanton background, the curvature is \star_q-self-dual. The Bogomolny decomposition yields

  \lVert F_\nabla \rVert^2 = c_2(A) + 2\lVert F_\nabla^- \rVert^2.

The instanton condition forces F_\nabla^- = 0, reducing the gauge sector to the topological term \mathcal{D}_\nabla^{2} = c_2(A). The categorical Lagrangian simplifies on-shell to

  \mathcal{L}_q\big|_{\text{instanton}} = c_2(A) + \psi^* \otimes \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi.

There are no dynamical gauge degrees of freedom beyond topology. All physics lies in the matter equation \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi = 0. The wavefront is determined by the background topology, dictating the Green's function of \mathcal{D}_\nabla.
rem:self-dual-ses:
Remark Self-duality as a short exact sequence. The q-Hodge star \star_q is an involution on \Omega^2(A). Its eigenspaces provide the splitting \Omega^2(A) = \Omega^+(A) \oplus \Omega^-(A) and the short exact sequence

  0 \to \Omega^-(A) \to \Omega^2(A) \to \Omega^+(A) \to 0,

where \Omega^{\pm}(A) = \ker(\mathrm{id} \mp \star_q). The instanton condition is exactly F_\nabla^- = 0. In the archimedean realisation, this specialises to 0 \to \Gamma(\Lambda^-\!H^* \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(P)) \to \Gamma(\Lambda^2 H^* \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(P)) \to \Gamma(\Lambda^+\!H^* \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(P)) \to 0.
rem:hopf-non-cocommutativity: Remark Non-cocommutativity of the Hopf structure. The Hopf comultiplication \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A of the Frobenius--Hopf object is coassociative but not cocommutative when q \neq 1. The failure is controlled by the universal R-matrix: \sigma \circ \Delta = \mathrm{Ad}_{R_q} \circ \Delta. This non-cocommutativity provides the algebraic origin of quantum uncertainty, preventing independent observations from commuting.
sec:dq-squared-intro: This section assesses the behaviour of the deformed differential d_q under iteration. The composition d_q^2 does not vanish in general; the obstruction is concentrated on non-Reeb-invariant forms. The q-connection forms the structural object whose curvature absorbs this obstruction.
prop:categorical-dq-squared:
Proposition Non-vanishing of d_q^2. The composition d_q^2 = d_q \circ d_q \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+2}(A) is given by

  d_q^2\alpha =  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\omega_V \wedge_q [\xi, \alpha],

where \omega_V \in \Omega^2(A) is the curvature of the weight decomposition and [\xi, \alpha] is the Lie derivative along the generator \xi.

The composition vanishes if and only if q = 1 or [\xi, \alpha] = 0. For generic \alpha with q \neq 1, d_q^2 \neq 0, so the q-deformed de Rham complex fails to be a cochain complex. On \xi-invariant horizontal forms, d_q reduces to q^{-1} d and d_q^2 = 0.
prf:categorical-dq-squared:
Proof Proof of Non-vanishing of d_q^2. Write a = q^{-1} and b = 1 - q^{-1}, so d_q = ad + b\pi_V d. Then

\begin{align*}
  d_q^2
  &= (ad + b\pi_V d)(ad + b\pi_V d) \\
  &= a^2\underbrace{d^2}_{= 0}
     + ab(d \circ \pi_V d + \pi_V d \circ d)
     + b^2\underbrace{\pi_V d \circ \pi_V d}_{= 0}.
\end{align*}

The first term vanishes because d^2 = 0 in the non-commutative de Rham complex. The last term vanishes because \pi_V is the projection onto the vertical (weight-1) summand of the Reeb decomposition \Omega^k(A) = \Omega^k_H(A) \oplus \varTheta_A \wedge \Omega^{k-1}_H(A): d applied to a vertical form produces one whose vertical component has weight \geq 2 in \varTheta_A, and the contact distribution forces \varTheta_A \wedge \varTheta_A = 0, so \pi_V(d(\pi_V\alpha)) = 0.

For the middle term, the commutator [d, \pi_V] measures how much d fails to preserve the weight grading. On a weight-n form \alpha_n, d\alpha_n = (d\alpha_n)_H + (d\alpha_n)_V, with the weight shift arising from the Lie derivative along \xi (the generator of T):

  [d, \pi_V]\alpha = \mathcal{L}_\xi(\alpha) - \pi_V(\mathcal{L}_\xi(\alpha))
  = \pi_H(\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha).

Using Cartan's formula \mathcal{L}_\xi = \iota_\xi \circ d + d \circ \iota_\xi and \pi_H + \pi_V = \mathrm{id}, the middle term simplifies to d(\pi_V d\alpha) + \pi_V d(d\alpha) = \omega_V \wedge_q [\xi, \alpha] where \omega_V = d(\pi_V(d1_A)) \in \Omega^2(A) is the curvature of the weight projection --- a canonical 2-form measuring the failure of the horizontal distribution to be integrable. \square
def:categorical-q-lie-bracket:
Definition Categorical q-Lie bracket. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. The q-deformed Lie bracket on derivations of A is

  [X, Y]_q =  q^{-1}[X, Y] + (1 - q^{-1})\bigl(\varTheta_A(X)[\xi, Y] - \varTheta_A(Y)[\xi, X]\bigr),

where \varTheta_A is the canonical 1-form dual to the Reeb derivation \xi.
def:categorical-q-connection:
Definition Categorical q-deformed connection. Let \nabla be a categorical connection on A and \xi the Reeb derivation. The q-deformed connection is

  \nabla_q =  q^{-1}\nabla + (1 - q^{-1})(\iota_\xi \nabla)\varTheta_A.
rem:categorical-q-connection-remark: Remark The undeformed limit of \nabla_q. At q = 1 the deformation term vanishes and \nabla_q = \nabla.
prop:categorical-q-connection-exists:
Proposition Existence of the categorical q-connection. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, au) be a quantum observable universe, with \mathbf{C} linear over the Laurent ring R_q, and let q \in R_q have inverse q^{-1}. Given morphisms

  
abla \colon A 	o A \otimes \Omega^1, \qquad
  \iota_\xi 
abla \colon A 	o A, \qquad
  	heta_
abla \colon A 	o A \otimes \Omega^1,

define

  
abla_q \;:=\; q^{-1}\,
abla \;+\; (1 - q^{-1})\,(\iota_\xi 
abla \mathbin{;} 	heta_
abla) \colon A 	o A \otimes \Omega^1 .

Then these data assemble into a categorical q-connection whose q-connection morphism is abla_q.

The existence is by construction: abla_q is defined by the formula above. That abla is a categorical connection in the sense of prop:categorical-connection-exists, and any property of abla_q beyond its formula, are not part of this statement.
prf:categorical-q-connection-exists: Proof Proof of existence of the categorical q-connection. \nabla exists by (existence of categorical connections). \iota_\xi \nabla \circ \varTheta is the composite of the connection with the Reeb interior product and the contact form — each a morphism in \mathbf{C}. The scalars q^{-1}, (1 - q^{-1}) give an R-linear combination, well-defined in any R-linear category.
prop:categorical-q-connection-unique: Proposition Uniqueness of the categorical q-connection. For fixed \nabla, \xi, \varTheta, and q, the categorical q-connection is uniquely determined. Up to gauge transformations, \nabla_q inherits the gauge freedom of its base connection \nabla.
prf:categorical-q-connection-unique: Proof Proof of uniqueness of the categorical q-connection. The formula \nabla_q = q^{-1} \nabla + (1 - q^{-1}) \iota_\xi \nabla \circ \varTheta is a fixed R-linear combination of uniquely-determined morphisms. Uniqueness of \nabla up to gauge (uniqueness of categorical connections) extends to \nabla_q through the linear map; the q-deformation does not introduce additional gauge freedom.
sec:q-deformed-operators-intro: The categorical q-deformed operators specialise to a concrete CR manifold M. The formulas below are recorded in classical differential-geometric language. Each operator inherits the uniform interpolation pattern q^{-1}(\text{classical}) + (1 - q^{-1})(\text{Reeb correction}).
ex:q-ext-deriv:
Example q-Deformed exterior derivative. In the archimedean realisation, the categorical d_q specialises to d_q \colon \Omega^k(M) \to \Omega^{k+1}(M):

  d_q\alpha = q^{-1}d\alpha + (1 - q^{-1})\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha.

The vertical projection \pi_V \circ d becomes \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi, and d_q^2 = q^{-1}(1-q^{-1})d\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi.
ex:q-lie-bracket:
Example q-Deformed Lie bracket. In the archimedean realisation, the categorical Reeb derivation induces the q-deformed Lie bracket on vector fields V, W \in \mathfrak{X}(M):

  [V, W]_q = q^{-1}[V, W] + (1 - q^{-1})\bigl(\varTheta(V)\mathcal{L}_\xi W - \varTheta(W)\mathcal{L}_\xi V\bigr).
ex:q-connection: Example q-Deformed connection. In the archimedean realisation, the categorical q-connection specialises to A_q = q^{-1}A + (1 - q^{-1})\iota_\xi A\varTheta. At q = 1, it recovers the full instanton connection A. As q \to \infty, it reduces to the Reeb component \iota_\xi A\varTheta.
ex:q-reeb-vector-field:
Example q-Deformed Reeb vector field. The categorical Reeb derivation \xi deforms in the archimedean setting to \xi_q, acting on smooth functions f \in C^\infty(M) by

  \xi_q(f) =  q^{-1}\xi(f) + (1 - q^{-1})[\xi, X_f]_q,

where X_f is the horizontal lift of \mathrm{grad}_{g_\varTheta}f to \ker\varTheta.
ex:q-reeb-flow:
Example q-Deformed Reeb flow. In the archimedean realisation, the q-deformed Reeb vector field \xi_q generates a one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms \phi_t^q \colon M \to M:

  \frac{d}{dt}\phi_t^q =  \xi_q \circ \phi_t^q, \qquad \phi_0^q = \mathrm{id}_M.
prop:aether-radial-coordinate:
Proposition Aether parameter as the radial coordinate. Within the contact affine chart U_\xi, the aether parameter q governs the radial coordinate. As q \to \infty in the deep-quantum limit, the affine coordinate Z \to 0. Conversely, as q \to 1 at the classical boundary, Z \to \infty. The q-deformed Reeb flow rotates the phase of Z according to:

  \mathcal{L}_\xi Z =  J\hbar_q Z,

where \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant and J is the complex structure on the horizontal distribution H.
prf:aether-radial-coordinate:
Proof Proof of aether radial coordinate. Within the contact affine chart U_\xi (contact affine chart), let Z be the affine coordinate of a state.

  1. Deep-quantum origin (Z \to 0): as q \to \infty (collapsing instanton), the state becomes purely vertical (\alpha_H \to 0). The affine coordinate vanishes, locating the primordial fermion at the origin of the chart.

  2. Classical boundary (Z \to \infty): as q \to 1 (classical vacuum), the state becomes purely horizontal (\iota_\xi\alpha \to 0, a boson). The affine coordinate diverges, pushing the state to the point at infinity of the \mathbb{CP}^1 fibre.

Furthermore, the q-deformed Reeb flow (the q-Reeb flow example) rotates the phase of Z at a rate proportional to the quantum Planck constant:

  \mathcal{L}_\xi Z = J\hbar_q Z,

where \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} (quantum Planck constant) and J is the complex structure on H.

Thus q controls the radial position in \mathbb{P}(V), with the bosonic sector at the boundary and the fermionic sector at the origin.
ex:q-torsion-leaf:
Example q-Torsion leaf. Let H = \ker\varTheta \subset TM be the horizontal distribution on the CR manifold M. A q-torsion leaf is a maximal integral submanifold L \hookrightarrow M of H invariant under the q-deformed Reeb flow:

  T_p L \subset H_p \quad\text{and}\quad \phi_t^q(L) = L.
rem:q-torsion-existence: Remark q-Torsion leaves: existence and Frobenius obstruction. Maximal integral submanifolds of H are Legendrian submanifolds. A q-torsion leaf is a Legendrian submanifold invariant under the q-deformed Reeb flow. For q > 1, the deformation generically breaks periodicity, demanding KAM-type persistence results. The failure of the Frobenius structure on H forces the dimension bound and gives q-torsion leaves their rigidity.
rem:quantum-torsion-motivation:
Remark \mathrm{SU}(2) action as quantum torsion. Classical torsion measures the failure of infinitesimal parallelograms to close. Quantum torsion measures the failure of the algebra of states to commute. The \mathrm{SU}(2) action on the Frobenius–Hopf object A dictates this twist.

The aether parameter q acts as a torsion index. At q = 1, quantum torsion vanishes, the \mathrm{SU}(2) action operates smoothly, and the algebra commutes. For q \neq 1, non-commutativity tightens the structure, forcing the q-deformed Reeb flow and its invariant leaves into rigid configurations.

The spinor sign rule follows. The first 360^\circ rotation addresses the physical state in space; the second 360^\circ completes the quantum torsion reset, unwinding the twist imposed by the \mathrm{SU}(2) action on the vortex-tube fibre of the state bundle.
